gates.title: C dynamic array/list and BFS/DFS; passing tests, clean memory checks, Git branch/merge conflict, reproducible clean clone. ENSAM work counts when it demonstrates the skill.
Eigenvalues, orthogonality, projections and least squares demonstrated before the SVD supplement.
SVD understood and checked before PCA.
Broadcasting/vectorization; least squares compared with np.linalg.lstsq; gradient checks; probability simulation with uncertainty explained.
Evaluation gate: protected test set, train/validation split, preprocessing and leakage checks before micrograd.
Linear/logistic regression from scratch; fair scikit-learn comparison; metrics, leakage checks and failed approaches reported.
A reproducible pretrained-model baseline is evaluated before optional GPU MODE or CS336 support.
CPU implementation and tests establish correctness before kernel work.
Profiling identifies a measured bottleneck before GPU kernel implementation.
Dataset/splits/permissions, baseline, tests, 2–3 ablations, measured bottleneck, documented limitation and readable README.

S1: One current roadmap; resume actual progress. ENSAM work counts toward the C project gate when it proves the skill.
The MIT trial has two Tuesday sessions (17 and 24 November); from 1 December it awaits a continuation decision.
S2: SVD follows linear-algebra foundations; PCA follows SVD.
Thursday practice alternates probability simulation and arrays/broadcasting/plots.
Summer1: Optional July–August plan, 12–15 h/week including career time. Enable it when you want to use it; it creates no catch-up debt.
S3: CS229 and MML are topic-specific references, not parallel mandatory courses.
Wasserman and ENSAM share Wednesday’s 60–90 minutes.
S4: Study priority: ENSAM → UDL → Huang → MiniTorch. Karpathy and GPU concepts are supports, not extra tracks. Do not rush every UDL chapter by June.

UDL routine: slides/notebook → 6–12 pages → derive key equation → predict one modification → run/test → capture failure and result in Obsidian. If stuck for three sessions, use a short lecture explanation, then return to UDL.
Every 2–3 MiniTorch labs, cross-check with Huang/PyTorch.
Summer2: One modest paper reproduction; finish a tagged MiniTorch release and measured report.
S5: Prince explains why; Raschka builds the model; Tunstall/Hugging Face teaches use/evaluation of pretrained models.
ONE capstone only. GPU kernels require CPU correctness and a measured bottleneck. RX 7900 XT: supported ROCm/Triton/HIP paths; no CUDA/cuBLAS benchmark claims without NVIDIA hardware.
S6: PFE takes priority. Independent study stays at zero.

roadmap.examPeak: At an exam peak the independent-study budget can be zero. Keep university study time; cancel optional sessions and move milestones forward without doubled hours.
